data.why: A street corner with a signal on its mast arm over the lane going away, its gray controller on the sidewalk and a woman waiting to cross. It opens close on one red lamp on a wire, then each fix lands on the signal itself (mast arm, green, controller, yellow, all-red, loops, button, battery, fire truck sensor) with the queue, the crash and the woman as the visible consequences; it ends with the woman stepping out on red.

sentences.text: If you hang a red lamp over a road, you have a traffic light.
But one small lamp is easy to miss, so cars roll through.
So you mount it on a mast arm with a backplate.
But the red never changes, so cars pile up.
So you add a green lamp, and cars go.
But the green never ends, and the woman cannot cross.
So you add a box that switches green to red.
This is a signal controller.
But the box jumps straight to red, and cars crash.
So you add a yellow lamp that warns drivers first.
But drivers racing the yellow shoot into the crosswalk.
So you hold every lamp red for a moment.
But at night, that red makes one lone car wait.
So you cut a wire loop that feels its metal.
But the loop feels only the first car, so lines grow.
So a second loop farther back stretches the green.
But longer greens keep the woman waiting on the corner.
So you add a button that she presses to cross.
But the button needs power, and a storm cuts it.
So you add a battery that keeps the lamps running.
But running lamps still stop a fire truck at the red.
So a sensor turns it green for the truck.
Now the lamp turns red, and the woman crosses.
Congratulations, you have built a traffic light.
